tasks.title: Add the `defect/v1` and `metrics/v1` schemas and the five `metrics.*` config keys
tasks.goal: Every later task writes or reads data shaped by these two schemas, and classification reads the five config keys, so they come first. `defect/v1` is the defect file's frontmatter as JSON; `metrics/v1` is the document `vloop metrics --json` prints, designed here in full (leaf keys included) so task 8 has a contract to conform to and task 9 a key list to document. Two existing expectations must change — `config list` gains five lines and `schema list` two names — and changing exactly those is required, not weakening.

references.why: 'Defects' (the frontmatter fields, their enums and defect/v1), 'vloop metrics' (the metrics/v1 top-level keys, milliseconds, unrounded money, null unknowns), the config-key paragraph under 'Line classification', and the Constraints item naming the only two expectations that may change

the schema conventions metrics/v1 and defect/v1 must follow: draft 2020-12, a `schema` property equal to the schema's own name, unknown keys allowed at every level, embedded and read only from the embedded FS
the config key table, list-key behaviour (comma-joined text, TOML array in the file, VLOOP_* override) and the invalid-value message the new keys reuse

acceptance: `vloop schema list` prints exactly defect/v1, iteration/v1, metrics/v1, proposal/v1, session/v1, state/v1, verdict/v1, one per line; the two documents live in `schemas/defect.v1.json` and `schemas/metrics.v1.json`, are draft 2020-12, embedded like the other five, and read only from the embedded FS.

defect/v1 requires id, brief, origin, found-by, kind, severity, status, fixed-by, case and created, and declares an optional task; its keys are the frontmatter's own (hyphenated `found-by`, `fixed-by`, as the brief's 'frontmatter as JSON' dictates). It also requires `schema` equal to `defect/v1`, per B2's convention (the JSON form `defect list --json` prints carries it; the file's frontmatter need not). Enums: origin brief|plan|work|env, found-by gate|review|operator|user, kind bug|spec-gap|gate|gate-gap|regression, severity low|medium|high|critical, status open|fixed|wontfix.

metrics/v1 requires `schema` (const metrics/v1), brief, run_id, status, merged, tasks, size, time, rate, cost, tokens, models, effort, defects, records, lead_time, permission_denials, iterations, iterations_per_closed and by_task, and declares every leaf a later task emits (delivered/churn per category and deletions, per-phase time in milliseconds with gates nullable, per-phase cost in unrounded USD and per 1,000 code lines, tokens input/output/cache read/cache creation and cache-hit ratio, per-phase models and effort, defect counts and removal efficiency, missing records, per-task rows). Keys are snake_case except where the brief names them otherwise; no `additionalProperties: false` or `unevaluatedProperties: false` anywhere in either schema.
internal/schema/testdata gains a valid and an invalid fixture for each new schema, and the existing table-driven schema tests cover them (a defect with found-by `martian` fails at `/found-by`).

Config keys `metrics.stacks`, `metrics.code`, `metrics.test`, `metrics.docs`, `metrics.excluded` follow `areas` in that order; all are lists, default empty, set as comma-joined text, stored as TOML arrays under `[metrics]`, overridable by VLOOP_METRICS_STACKS … VLOOP_METRICS_EXCLUDED, printed by `config list` as `metrics.code=a,b (file)` and by `--json` as arrays. The four glob keys accept any non-empty doublestar-style pattern (e.g. `internal/brief/templates/**`); `areas` still rejects anything that is not a lower-case name. Validating `metrics.stacks` against the preset names is task 2's, not this task's.

The only pre-existing test expectations changed are the `config list` output (five `metrics.*` lines added) and the `schema list` output (defect/v1 and metrics/v1 added), in internal/cli, internal/schema and cmd/vloop; no other assertion is removed or loosened. README's configuration table lists the five keys and their variables so B1's README test still passes.

tasks.title: Build line classification: the stack presets, the layers, `vloop metrics stacks` and `vloop metrics classify`
tasks.goal: Every line count in this slice is a count per category, and the category comes from here: the repo's own globs first, then the presets `metrics.stacks` names, then `other`, with `.vloop/**` and `.loop/**` always excluded. The preset table is product data shipped in the binary — a preset that exists only in a test is a violation. File extension alone is not enough: vloop's own brief templates are `.md` files that are product code, which is why the repo's globs win.

references.why: 'Line classification — vloop metrics stacks and vloop metrics classify': the nine presets glob for glob, the layer order, the `always` layer, and the exact output and error formats of both commands
'Metrics and defects' → Size: why globs rather than extensions, and that presets merge while the repo's globs win; the brief's table wins where the two differ

acceptance: An `internal/classify` package holds the nine presets (csharp, go, java, javascript, kotlin, python, react, rust, typescript) exactly as the brief's table lists them — code, test and excluded globs in the table's order, docs `**/*.md` for every preset — as Go data in non-test code; `vloop metrics stacks` and task 9's guide read them from there.

Classification uses github.com/bmatcuk/doublestar/v4 (the only new module) against the repo-relative `/` path; `.vloop/**` and `.loop/**` are `excluded` before any layer (layer name `always`); then the repo's `metrics.excluded`, `metrics.test`, `metrics.docs`, `metrics.code` in that order (layer `repo`); then every named preset's excluded, then every test, then every docs, then every code (layer = the preset name, presets taken in `metrics.stacks` order); else `other` with `(none)`.

`vloop metrics stacks` prints the preset names sorted, one per line; `vloop metrics stacks <name>` prints `code:`, `test:`, `docs:`, `excluded:` each followed by its globs indented two spaces; `--json` prints `{name: {code, test, docs, excluded}}` for all presets or the named one; an unknown name prints `vloop: unknown stack "<name>"` on stderr, nothing on stdout, exit 2.
`vloop metrics classify <path>…` prints `<path>  <category>  (<layer>: <glob>)` per path, or `<path>  other  (none)`, exit 0; it matches the brief's worked example line for line.

`vloop config set metrics.stacks cobol` exits 2 with B1's invalid-value message (`vloop: invalid value "cobol" for metrics.stacks: want …`) and writes nothing; valid names are the preset names, taken from the classify package rather than a second list.

Committed tests: `TestPreset…` and `TestLayer…` in internal/classify with a fixture per preset and per layer, each with a path where it applies and one where it must not; CLI tests in internal/cli/classify_test.go; the README documents `vloop metrics stacks` and `vloop metrics classify` so B1's README test passes.

tasks.goal: Every metric is derived from run folders, commits and the plan in git; this task turns both layouts — the shell loop's `.loop/state/runs/` with `[loop]` commits, and B6's future `.vloop/state/runs/` with `[vloop]` commits — into one per-brief model the later tasks compute over. Metrics are keyed by brief, not by folder: a brief spans several runs and its plan session can sit under another branch's folder. vloop only reads here; it never writes under `.loop/`. There is no CLI surface yet, so this task's committed tests are its whole proof until task 8's gate plays the worked example end to end.

the shell loop's actual telemetry: `run_session` (session record = claude JSON plus phase and iteration, named NNN-<phase>.json by sequence not iteration), iteration outcomes done/blocked/gate_fail/review_fail, the loop.log lines and the commit subjects
session/v1, iteration/v1 and verdict/v1 field names, and gate_history, which the vloop layout carries

acceptance: A package `internal/runs` resolves a brief (path or name) to its run id (name minus `.loop-brief`) and collects every run folder that belongs to it: shell-loop folders at `.loop/state/runs/<any>/<folder>/` whose loop.log, ANSI colour stripped, contains `planning from <brief path>` or `resuming <run id>` (folders with neither are ignored), and vloop folders at `.vloop/state/runs/<run id>/<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>/`.

It reads sessions (`sessions/NNN-<phase>.json`: shell-loop cost `total_cost_usd`, time `duration_ms`, models and tokens from `modelUsage`, `permission_denials`, phase and iteration; session/v1 equivalents), iterations (`iterations.jsonl`, shell-loop and iteration/v1, gate durations where present) and verdicts (`reports/NNN-verdict.json`, shell-loop string findings and verdict/v1 findings with kind) into one model; a session's task comes from the iteration it names.

Owned commits come from every local ref: the latest `[loop] plan <run id>` / `[vloop] plan <run id>` commit, the last `run <run id>/…` commit after it on the same history, and the `<task>: <outcome>` commits between them; an earlier plan commit (a re-plan) and its commits do not count. tasks.title: Count lines: delivered and churn per category, deletions, rework and test:code
tasks.goal: Size is the headline of every metric the operator compares, and the counting rule is easy to get subtly wrong: added non-blank lines per category, deletions apart, binary files and `.loop/`/`.vloop/` paths never counted, renames only for their content change. Delivered is one diff (plan commit's parent to the last run commit); churn is the sum over the brief's task commits whatever their outcome, per task as well as in total, which is what `--by task` shows. There is no CLI yet; task 8's gate replays the worked example's 15/17 against this code.

references.why: 'What is counted' — Lines, Delivered, Churn, Rework, Test:code — and the worked example's size row (code 15 delivered, 17 churn, rework 1.13, test:code 0.40) the numbers must reproduce by those rules

acceptance: Lines are added non-blank lines of a git diff (a line of only whitespace is blank), classified per path by task 2's classifier into code/test/docs/other; deleted lines are reported separately; binary files are not counted; a rename counts only its content change; anything classified `excluded` (including every `.loop/**` and `.vloop/**` path) is never counted.

Delivered = the diff from the plan commit's parent to the brief's last run commit. Churn = the sum over the brief's `<task>:` commits, whatever the outcome, kept per task and in total. tasks.title: Compute time, cost, tokens, models, task counts, first-pass and missing records
tasks.goal: These are the numbers that say what a brief cost and how long it took, and B1's and B2's real telemetry pins several of them to the cent, so the aggregation rules matter more than the formatting. Summing unrounded session values is the rule (the hand-rounded run records disagree with the telemetry and the telemetry wins), and a missing session record is reported rather than silently shrinking the totals. No CLI yet; task 8 and the close check these end to end.

references.why: 'What is counted' — Time, Rates, Cost, Models, Tasks, Missing records — plus the worked example (agent 2.7 min, $2.10, first-pass 1/2) and the real-data numbers for B1 and B2 these rules must reproduce

acceptance: Agent time = work + review session durations; plan time is reported apart; gate time is the sum of iteration/v1 gate durations and unknown (null, shown `n/a`) for the shell loop; wall time = plan commit's committer time to the last run commit's. Rates use agent time: delivered code lines per minute, and code + test.

Cost per phase and total are sums of unrounded session costs (rounding only at display); cost per 1,000 delivered code lines; tokens input, output, cache read and cache creation summed, cache-hit ratio = cache read / (input + cache read + cache creation). Models per phase are the distinct models in the sessions' model usage, sorted and comma-joined; effort per phase where session/v1 records carry it.

Tasks: planned, done and blocked are counted in the plan at the last run commit; first-pass = tasks whose only iteration outcome is `done`; the estimate is the brief's `<n> to <m> tasks` phrase (absent when the brief states none); iterations per closed task is also computed.

tasks.title: Detect release and add `vloop defect add|list|set` with `--blame` attribution
tasks.goal: Defects the loop cannot see — found by the operator before merge or by users after release — are recorded as one file each under `.vloop/defects/`, and `--blame` attributes one to the brief that introduced the line so nobody has to remember which run wrote it. Release is detected, never declared: the brief's first default-branch commit where its frontmatter says `status: consumed`. The default branch is origin/HEAD's target, else main, else master — the same resolution blame uses.

references.why: 'Defects' → Recorded by the operator: the file name and format, `defect add|list|set` flags, slug rule, collision suffix, `--blame` resolution and its exact stderr and error lines, and the exit codes; 'What is counted' → Release
global flags, `--json`, exit codes 0/1/2, one-line `vloop: ` errors and the invalid-value message the enum flags reuse

acceptance: `vloop defect add "<summary>" --found-by <c> [--brief] [--task] [--origin work] [--kind bug] [--severity medium] [--case] [--blame <file>:<line>]` writes `.vloop/defects/D<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>-<slug>.md` (local time; slug = summary lower-cased, each run of non-alphanumerics as `-`, at most 40 characters; `-2`, `-3`… before `.md` on collision, never overwriting), YAML frontmatter in the brief's field order then the summary as the description, and prints the repo-relative path on stdout.

`--blame <file>:<line>` (used when `--brief` is absent) runs `git blame` on the line on the default branch (origin/HEAD's target, else main, else master — not HEAD); the commit's `Vloop-Brief: <name>` trailer names the brief, else the loop brief whose frontmatter became `status: consumed` in that commit; stderr gets `attributed to <name> (trailer on <sha7>)` or `(consumed in <sha7>)`. Unattributable: `vloop: cannot attribute <file>:<line> to a loop brief — pass --brief`, exit 1, nothing written.

tasks.title: Derive defects from runs, reclassify through `gate_history`, and print the origin × catcher matrix
tasks.goal: The loop's own catches are defects too, and counting only the files would make removal efficiency meaningless; this task derives them from the run on every call — never stored — so a later `task verify` reclassifies without a migration. A gate can itself be the defect: a gate failure before an operator's `gate_history` entry on that task is the plan's fault, not the work's. The matrix and removal efficiency are the headline numbers the operator reads.

references.why: 'Defects' → Derived by vloop (gate_fail/gate_failed, review_fail/rejected per finding with kind mapping, the gate_history rule, blocked not a defect), the matrix layout, and Counting (in-loop, operator, escaped, removal efficiency)
'Metrics and defects' → the origin and catcher axes and 'A gate can be the defect'; the brief wins where the two differ
gate_history's fields (verify, replaced_at, reason, by operator|planner) that the reclassification reads

acceptance: Each `gate_fail` (shell loop) / `gate_failed` (vloop) iteration is one derived defect: origin work, kind bug, found-by gate. Each `review_fail` / `rejected` iteration is one defect per verdict finding (kind from a verdict/v1 finding — origin brief for spec-gap, plan for gate-gap, work otherwise; kind bug for the shell loop's string findings), or one defect when the list is empty; found-by review. `blocked` iterations are not defects.

A gate failure on a task before an entry in that task's `gate_history` with `by: operator` becomes origin plan, kind gate; an entry by `planner`, or on another task, reclassifies nothing. Derived defects are recomputed on every call and never written to disk.

`vloop defect list --matrix [--brief <name>]` prints the origin (brief, plan, work, env) × catcher (gate, review, operator, user) counts for the selected briefs (all briefs with runs when none is given), derived defects included, in the brief's layout; plain `defect list` still shows only recorded defects.

Counting: in-loop = found-by gate or review (derived and recorded), operator, escaped = user; removal efficiency = (in-loop + operator) / all as a whole percentage, or `n/a` with no defects — computed here, printed by task 8.

Committed tests `TestDerived…`, `TestMatrix…` and `TestRemovalEfficiency…` in internal/metrics (plus internal/cli/matrix_test.go) cover every rule with a fixture where it applies and one where it must not, both layouts, temporary directories only; README documents `--matrix`.

tasks.title: Add `vloop metrics`: the per-brief summary, `--by task`, the cross-brief table and `--json`
tasks.goal: This is the command the whole slice exists for: it assembles tasks 3–7 into the summary the brief pins line by line, the per-task table, a cross-brief table, and a `metrics/v1` document. The gate replays the brief's worked example on a fixture repository and a second fixture in vloop's own layout; a number that matches one fixture by a different computation is a violation, so every figure must come from the rule the brief states. `vloop metrics` writes nothing.

references.why: 'vloop metrics [<brief>…] [--by task] [--json]' — the summary template, the rounding and separators, `--by task` columns, the cross-brief columns, `no runs` error, metrics/v1 top-level keys — and the worked example and planted failures the output must reproduce
the fuller shape the summary and tables come from (not a contract: where it differs from the brief, the brief wins — e.g. no rule line, `docs+` column, `$/1k`)

acceptance: `vloop metrics <brief>` (path or name) prints the brief's summary template: `<run id>  <status> · merged <sha7>` (or `· not merged`), then tasks, size (delivered and churn rows), time, rate, cost, models, defects rows, and a `records` row only when records are missing; `(brief said <n>–<m>)` only when the brief states an estimate; minutes and ratios to the decimals the worked example shows, money to two, counts with `,` thousands separators. On the worked example it matches the brief line for line with spaces collapsed.

`--by task` prints `id  area  kind  att  code+  test+  docs+  other+  agent  cost  model` with one row per task in plan order: att = its iterations, line columns = its churn, agent `XmYYs`, `-` for a missing area or kind.

With no brief: a header `brief  tasks  first-pass  code  test  t:c  agent  $/1k  in-loop  operator  escaped  efficiency` and one row per brief that has runs, in name order (run id, agent in minutes, cost per 1,000 delivered code lines). A brief with no runs: `vloop: no runs for <name>` on stderr, exit 1.

`--json` prints one metrics/v1 document per brief (an array when several), validating against the embedded schema: durations in milliseconds, money unrounded, unknowns null, `iterations_per_closed` a number.

Every figure comes from tasks 3–7's rules (e.g. cost per 1,000 lines is total cost / delivered code × 1000, gate time from iteration/v1, missing records excluded from time and cost) — not from a formula that happens to match the fixture. `vloop metrics` writes nothing to the working tree.

Committed `TestMetricsCommand…` tests in internal/cli cover the summary, `--by task`, the cross-brief table, `--json` and `no runs` on temporary fixtures; README documents `vloop metrics` and `--by`; none of B4's work (`brief close`, run records, a metrics snapshot, `metrics export`, `--workspace`) appears.
